summary: Develop covers building, customizing, publishing and maintaining Business Central apps and extensions. It answers questions on getting started as a partner, Marketplace submission and validation, embed apps, app lifecycle, localization, and Microsoft versus partner responsibilities online.
overview:
The Develop section is for partners and developers who tailor Business Central or build apps for the Microsoft commercial marketplace. It ranges from customizing a tenant with the in-client Designer or AL extensions, to building Connect and Add-on apps, localization solutions, and embed apps.

Start with "The SMB opportunity for app publishers" for the business context and app types, then "Get started building apps" for partner registration, publisher setup, object range and submission to Partner Center. "Components and capabilities" shows integration options such as APIs, Power BI, Power Automate and Power Apps.

For submission and upkeep, use "Add your App to Marketplace" and the Marketplace validation subtopic for the technical and marketing checklists. After release, the lifecycle, maintenance and Microsoft responsibilities pages explain updates, breaking changes and who runs what. "Discontinuing a Marketplace App" covers removal. The Embed apps subtopic covers partner-branded solutions.
key_points: Customize a tenant with the in-client Designer for UI changes, or with AL extensions (page and table extensions, business logic) in Visual Studio Code. Test in sandbox or Docker first.
Getting started on Marketplace involves becoming a partner, registering as a publisher, getting a unique object range, building the solution and submitting through Partner Center.

Marketplace submission needs both technical and marketing validation. The Marketplace validation subtopic has 15 pages, including checklists, landing page and video guidance, and a technical validation FAQ.
Apps can integrate through the Dynamics 365 API endpoint, Outlook Add-in, Power BI, Power Automate, Power Apps and Azure Machine Learning.

Lifecycle pages cover service updates, app updates, bug fixes, breaking changes and extension data retention. Publishers and resellers must keep Marketplace apps and per-tenant extensions compatible with major and minor releases. The AppSourceCop analyzer, preview testing and enforcement periods support this.

Microsoft handles infrastructure, storage, high availability, disaster recovery, platform security, diagnostics and patching, plus the base application. Partners maintain their own apps and extensions.
Localization apps address local regulatory requirements and national standards. They can use RapidStart data packages, translations and setup guides.
Embed apps are partner-branded solutions. Their pages cover partner qualification, application family name in URLs, LCS deployment, customer access management and the App Management API.
